short: The name Nervii is associated with that part of Gaul, which is now northeastern France and Belgium, as, for example, Dux tractus Armoricani et Nervicani in Notitia. The name comes from the ancient Gallic tribe after which the area was named: the Nervii, but from Tacitus we learn that according to the version of the Nervii themselves, their tribe had Germanic roots. «The Treveri and Nervii claim a Germanic origin and, moreover, are proud of it, as if the boast of such affinity could save them from their similarity to the Gauls and the inherent weakness of those». During the period of the early empire a large number of auxiliary units were recruited from this area, some of which survived long enough to appear in Notitia, such as those listed in Dux Britanniarum. This area later became known as the Civitas Nerviorum; presumably Nervian units were recruited from this region. Milites (latin) «servicemen, soldiers» were trained regular infantrymen in the Roman army, and later this term was also used to describe «soldiers» in Medieval Europe. Milites are set in contrast to tirones (latin tiro, tironis), recruits in the armies of the Roman Empire. In this status they were until six months after joining the legion, and only after completing the training, began to be considered milites - regular legionnaires.
history: In the face of an increasing number of barbarian incursions, the effective defence of Rome’s now-sprawling territory became a serious problem in the 4th century AD. The Emperor Constantine’s controversial solution was to divide the army into two halves. 'Limitanei', literally ‘the men on the limes’ or 'borders', were frontier garrison troops intended to pin down an invading force until the full-time 'comitatenses', the late-Roman equivalent of the traditional Legionaries, could arrive to deal with the situation decisively. Although well-equipped, limitanei were generally considered by all to be second-class warriors. This was possibly because they were often part-time soldiers who had been encouraged to settle and farm the land around their outposts in exchange for policing the Empire's borders.
strengths: Very low damage and armour penetration
